_comment: Paragraph three: the pattern behind today, in this part of your life.
And the one-line mechanism note that sits in the measurement row.
pattern    area x tone   45   the recurring shape, and the trap
mechanism  tone  5             what this kind of angle is
mechanism  transit 10          how long it lasts
── What this file used to be, and why it changed ──
It held three encyclopaedia entries, keyed by natal point, tone and
transit, concatenated into one paragraph. Twenty-seven sentences total,
a hundred and six words, sixty-three per cent of every expanded card,
and the same text for every reader forever. Its middle fragment had five
entries, so one of them printed six hundred times a year for one person,
and on thirty-six per cent of cards it repeated a sentence already shown
on another card the same morning. Three cards into a morning you had
read what a hard angle is three times.
None of that was rescuable by rewriting, because the address had no area
in it. A paragraph that must be true whether the card says Money or Home
can only describe the machinery.
The mechanical content did not need a paragraph anyway. The measurement
row directly underneath already prints the two bodies, the aspect, both
signs, the degrees off and the orb allowed. So the encyclopaedia is now
one short line inside that row, where the vocabulary belongs, and this
paragraph became reader-facing prose about the area.
── The three paragraphs, and their three time horizons ──
1  today          readings.json    what is happening, and what to do
2  always         placements.json  the permanent thing that makes it land here
3  every time     this file        the recurring pattern, and the usual mistake
That is what keeps three area-keyed paragraphs from collapsing into one
another. They are the same subject at three distances. If a pattern entry
reads like an instruction for today, it has drifted into paragraph one's
job and the seams suite will fail it on overlap.
── Rules ──
Plain language, second person, no astrology, no planet names. Say what
this kind of day does in this area over time and name the mistake people
make in it. Full rules in CORPUS-RULES.md section 8.

self.charged: Days like this are about visibility rather than about achievement. You have not changed, the light has. The mistake is treating the extra attention as a verdict and adjusting yourself to keep it.
self.open: The openings in this part of your life are never announced. Nothing here arrives unasked, which is why these days pass unnoticed more than any other kind. What you do not ask for stays exactly where it was.
self.friction: Friction here almost always arrives as a misreading rather than as a conflict. Somebody has the wrong picture of you. The trap is arguing with the picture, which makes it look accurate and makes you look worried about it.
self.easy: Ease in this part of your life is social rather than practical. Being around you costs people less. It is the easiest thing in the world to spend that on people who already like you, which is also the only way to waste it.
self.pull: This part of your life splits when who you are and who you are expected to be stop matching. Both are real. The failure is running both at once, which produces a third version nobody recognises, including you.

money.charged: Days like this in this part of your life turn on a figure becoming visible. The number was always there. What changes is that you have to look at it or say it, and the discomfort is about the saying rather than about the amount.
money.open: Openings in this part of your life are small and short: a rate, a request, a piece of admin that is briefly painless. None of it feels significant at the time. The ones you take are worth more in a year than anything you agonised over.
money.friction: Money trouble here is almost never about the total. It is about arithmetic you have not done, or a decision you have been making by feel. The trap is solving a spreadsheet problem with a mood, or the reverse.
money.easy: When earning is easy here, the temptation is to enjoy it rather than build on it. The rate you can get today is not the rate you get all year. What you set up now is what carries the flat months.
money.pull: This part of your life splits over which currency you are paying in: money, time, or goodwill. You have more of one than you think and less of another, and pretending you can spend all three is how a month goes wrong.

talk.charged: Days like this amplify whatever was already being said. Nothing new arrives. What was subtle becomes obvious, which is useful if you meant it and expensive if you were relying on it staying subtle.
talk.open: The opening in this part of your life is always a message somebody is waiting for, and it stays open for about a day. These pass unnoticed because sending it feels too small to count as having done anything.
talk.friction: Trouble in this part of your life is a misunderstanding rather than a disagreement, nine times in ten: you and somebody else using one word to mean two things. The trap is explaining harder, which entrenches both definitions instead of finding the gap.
talk.easy: When talking comes easily to you, the words are there for the difficult conversation rather than for the pleasant one, which was going to go fine anyway. Days like this are how your backlog of them gets cleared.
talk.pull: This part of your life splits between being liked and being clear. The message that keeps everybody comfortable does not say the thing. You will spend one of the two, and choosing is better than finding out afterwards.

home.charged: Days like this bring something domestic to the front of your attention, out of all proportion to its size. The object is rarely the subject. What is loud is something that went unresolved long enough to become furniture.
home.open: The openings here are small and physical: a room, an errand, an invitation. None of them look like progress. They are the ones that quietly change how the rest of your month feels to live in.
home.friction: Friction here runs on an old script, with everybody playing the part they were cast in years ago, including you. The trap is trying to rewrite a decades-old arrangement in one evening, which is how the same argument gets had again.
home.easy: When this part of your life is easy, rest actually restores rather than merely passing time, and that does not happen most weeks. The failure is spending the day productively and wondering why the tiredness is still there tomorrow.
home.pull: This part of your life splits between where you are from and where you are going. Both have a claim and neither is wrong. Being half present in both places is worse for everybody than being honestly absent from one.

making.charged: Days like this bring an idea to the front whether or not the timing suits you, and it will not wait politely. The trap is treating the arrival as a plan, when the arrival is all it is.
making.open: Openings here look like play rather than like work: an hour of messing about, a technique tried sideways, a tangent followed. That is how a stuck thing comes loose in this part of your life, and it never feels like progress at the time.
making.friction: What stops you here is almost never a block. It is an unfinished section wearing a block's clothes. The trap is polishing the part that already works, which feels like effort and moves nothing at all.
making.easy: When this comes easily, the temptation is to coast through the parts that were never hard. Ease here is for spending on the difficult section. A day like this used on the easy half is a day you will want back.
making.pull: This part of your life splits between the thing you want to make and the thing you owe. Both are real work and only one is on a list. The failure is giving the wanted one whatever time is left, because there is never time left.

work.charged: Days like this bring your visibility and your output into the same frame. Somebody is forming a view, and it is being built out of small visible things rather than out of the quality of what you actually did.
work.open: Openings here are almost always somebody's willingness to say yes, and it does not last the week. The ask is smaller than the case you were preparing. Most of these close because nobody asked in time.
work.friction: What blocks you here is structural rather than personal, nearly always: a bad process wearing somebody's face. The trap is working harder at a thing that is actually waiting on a decision nobody has made.
work.easy: The good stretches here are shorter than they feel and they never announce themselves. Whatever is already in front of you will happily absorb one, and a month later the difficult piece is exactly where it was. That is the whole failure mode.
work.pull: This part of your life splits between doing the work and being seen doing it. Both are real and they want different hours. Whichever one you have been starving this month is the one to feed.

love.charged: Days like this put something unspoken at the centre of everything between you, and nobody has to mention it for it to be the subject. The trap is managing around it for another week rather than saying it in one sentence.
love.open: The openings here are small: an invitation, a plain question, a specific plan. They look too minor to matter. Every large thing in this part of your life started as one of them, and they close within a day or two.
love.friction: Trouble here is usually with somebody who is not in the room, an old pattern applied to a current person. The trap is testing them for it, because you will not believe the result whichever way it comes out.
love.easy: When this part of your life is easy, the difficult conversation goes well and the pleasant one would have gone fine anyway. That is the whole opportunity and it does not hold. The waste is spending it on the person who was never the problem.
love.pull: This part of your life splits between comfort and wanting, or between two people who need different amounts of you. Averaging satisfies nobody. Say what you can actually offer and let them decide from that.

sex.charged: Days like this bring appetite and closeness into the same room and make them hard to tell apart. Charge is not intimacy. Notice which of the two you are actually getting before you decide anything on the strength of it.
sex.open: The opening here is somebody's willingness to hear your honest version without it turning into a whole conversation. It is rare and it is short. What does not get said now gets considerably harder to say next week.
sex.friction: What goes wrong for you here is about who decides rather than about whatever is being discussed, and that stays true even when the subject is money or time. The trap is winning the surface argument and leaving the real one untouched.
sex.easy: When this part of your life is easy, the distance between you costs less to cross than usual and moving first is cheap. The waste is waiting for the other person to do it, which is what cost you the last few weeks.
sex.pull: This part of your life splits over what is yours and what is shared: money, time, secrets, or the right to decide. The failure is leaving the boundary unspoken until it can only come out as an accusation.

belief.charged: Days like this put a position of yours in front of a fact that does not fit it, and the mismatch is the useful part. The trap is defending the position on the day, before you have seen which of the two survives.
belief.open: Openings here are the ones that look optional: a book, a booking, a question asked of somebody older. Nothing forces you into them. That is exactly why they get left, and why a year of yours can pass looking much like the last one.
belief.friction: Trouble here is usually you arguing with something that was never reasoned into place, so it will not be reasoned out. The trap is spending real effort on an audience of one who is not listening.
belief.easy: When this part of your life is easy, the long view is unusually clear and the week stops being the unit. Decisions that are impossible up close make themselves from a distance. Clarity like this does not sit still for long.
belief.pull: This part of your life splits between what you believe and what the evidence says, or between growing and staying put. Both sides are real. The failure is settling it by looking away rather than by setting a date where one of them wins.

tone.charged: Two bodies in the same degree, which amplifies rather than pushing in any direction.
tone.open: A soft angle: available rather than forced, and only for as long as it holds.
tone.friction: A hard angle between two parts of a chart that both want the same day.
tone.easy: The easiest angle there is, which is why it can pass without being spent.
tone.pull: Two parts of your chart at opposite ends of one line, both of them yours.

transit.moon: Thirteen degrees a day, so this forms and breaks inside a few hours.
transit.sun: About a degree a day, so it runs two or three days and comes back once a year.
transit.mercury: About a degree a day, and it doubles back, so this is short and can repeat within a season.
transit.venus: A few days. Long enough to be a mood, short enough to wait out.
transit.mars: The better part of a week, long enough for a mood to turn into a decision.
transit.jupiter: About a month to cross, so this is a season of something rather than a day of it.
transit.saturn: A couple of degrees a year, so it has been forming for months and clears over months.
transit.uranus: Slow to arrive and abrupt when it does, so the contact spans months and the events do not.
transit.neptune: Less than a degree in a season, so this is weather rather than a day.
transit.pluto: About two arcseconds a day, so this spans seasons and can return two or three times.
